original.title: The German alphabet and sounds
explanation: German has 26 letters like English, plus ä, ö, ü and ß. The dots on ä, ö, ü change the sound. ß is a sharp 's' that comes after a long vowel, as in 'heißen'.

Some letters sound different from English. Z sounds like 'ts', W sounds like English 'v', and V usually sounds like English 'f' (as in 'vier'). The letters ei sound like English 'eye' ('nein'). The letters ie sound like a long 'ee' ('Wiedersehen'). Sch sounds like 'sh', and ch is a soft breath sound ('ich') or a rough sound at the back of the throat ('Nacht').
To spell a name (buchstabieren), say each letter name one after the other: 'Lena' is L – E – N – A. You can ask: 'Wie buchstabiert man das?'

explanation: Pronouns replace names. ich = I, du = you (one friend), er = he, sie = she, wir = we. In German the verb changes its ending after each pronoun.

explanation: Numbers 0 to 12 are new words you learn by heart: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf. Then 13 to 19 use the ending -zehn: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn. Watch out: sechzehn (not sechszehn) and siebzehn (not siebenzehn).
The tens are: zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig, neunzig, hundert. Note dreißig (30), sechzig (60) and siebzig (70).

From 21 to 99 the order is the opposite of English: first the unit, then und, then the tens, all written as one word. 21 = einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty). With 1, you say ein, not eins: einunddreißig.
To say your age, use sein: Ich bin 25 Jahre alt. Ask with: Wie alt bist du? For phone numbers, say the digits one by one or in pairs: 0151 – null eins fünf eins.

intro.title: Numbers 0–100, phone numbers and age
explanation: Numbers 0 to 12 are new words you learn by heart: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf. Then 13 to 19 use the ending -zehn: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn. Watch out: sechzehn (not sechszehn) and siebzehn (not siebenzehn).
The tens are: zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig, neunzig, hundert. Note dreißig (30), sechzig (60) and siebzig (70).

From 21 to 99 the order is the opposite of English: first the unit, then und, then the tens, all written as one word. 21 = einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty). With 1, you say ein, not eins: einunddreißig.
To say your age, use sein: Ich bin 25 Jahre alt. Ask with: Wie alt bist du? For phone numbers, say the digits one by one or in pairs: 0151 – null eins fünf eins.
